diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Hemileia vastatrix.
diseases.symptoms: Yellow to orange-yellow powdery rust spots appear mainly on the underside of leaves. Severe infection can cause premature leaf fall and reduced plant vigour.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected leaves where practical and improve canopy ventilation. Use locally recommended rust-management fungicides only when disease pressure warrants treatment, following the current label and local agricultural advisory.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant or tolerant varieties where available, maintain good shade and canopy management, remove heavily affected material, and monitor plants regularly during favourable humid conditions.

diseases.cause: Bacterial disease commonly associated with Xanthomonas species.
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked to dark lesions may occur on leaves, veins, stems and bolls. Lesions can enlarge and cause leaf damage and boll infection.
diseases.treatment: Remove heavily infected plant material and maintain field sanitation. Use healthy seed and resistant or tolerant varieties where available. If chemical management is recommended locally, follow the current crop-specific agricultural advisory and product label.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed and resistant/tolerant varieties where available, maintain field sanitation, avoid unnecessary leaf wetness, and monitor fields regularly.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by powdery-mildew fungi.
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth appears on leaf surfaces and may spread over larger portions of the foliage. Severe infection can reduce photosynthetic activity.
diseases.treatment: Improve canopy ventilation and avoid excessive nitrogen. Remove severely affected material where practical. If disease pressure is significant, use a locally recommended fungicide according to the current label and agricultural advisory.
diseases.prevention: Maintain appropriate plant spacing and canopy ventilation, avoid excessive nitrogen, remove heavily infected material where practical, and monitor during favourable weather.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
diseases.symptoms: Circular brown lesions develop on leaves, often showing concentric rings resembling a target. Lesions may enlarge and cause premature defoliation.
diseases.treatment: Remove or manage infected crop residue and improve canopy airflow. Monitor lower leaves for early disease development. Where fungicide treatment is recommended, use only a currently approved product at its crop-specific label rate.
diseases.prevention: Use good field sanitation, maintain adequate plant spacing and airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and monitor lower leaves for early symptoms.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease associated with Cercospora species.
diseases.symptoms: Small brown to grey leaf spots develop and may enlarge or merge under favourable conditions, reducing healthy leaf area.
diseases.treatment: Use healthy seed and maintain field sanitation. Improve crop ventilation and avoid excessive crop density. If disease becomes significant, follow the locally recommended fungicide programme and current product label.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, maintain field sanitation, avoid excessive crop density, and monitor the crop during warm and humid weather.

diseases.cause: Viral disease associated with a whitefly-transmitted begomovirus complex.
diseases.symptoms: Leaves develop yellow or golden mosaic patterns. Infected plants may show reduced growth and abnormal foliage.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected plants early where recommended and use healthy planting material. Manage the whitefly vector through integrated pest management. Use vector-management products only when necessary and according to current local recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy planting material, remove infected plants early where recommended, control vector populations through integrated management, and maintain field sanitation.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Bipolaris oryzae.
diseases.symptoms: Brown circular to oval spots appear on leaves and may also occur on other plant parts. Severe infection can reduce leaf function and grain quality.
diseases.treatment: Maintain balanced crop nutrition, use healthy seed and manage field sanitation. When fungicide treatment is necessary, use a currently recommended rice fungicide according to the local agricultural advisory and product label. ICAR advisories have specifically included mancozeb for brown-spot management.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed and suitable varieties, maintain balanced nutrition, avoid nutrient stress, remove infected crop residues where practical, and monitor regularly.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Entyloma oryzae.
diseases.symptoms: Small dark greenish to black lesions or smut-like spots develop on leaves, particularly under favourable humid conditions.
diseases.treatment: Use healthy seed, maintain field sanitation and balanced nutrition, and monitor the crop regularly. If disease pressure warrants treatment, use only a locally recommended fungicide according to its current rice label.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, maintain field sanitation and balanced crop nutrition, avoid excessive nitrogen, and monitor fields for early symptoms.

diseases.cause: Viral disease caused by sugarcane mosaic virus complexes.
diseases.symptoms: Leaves show characteristic light and dark green mosaic or mottling. Severely affected plants may have reduced growth and yield.
diseases.treatment: Use healthy, disease-free planting material and resistant or tolerant varieties where available. Rogue and destroy clearly infected plants where recommended and manage vectors using integrated methods. Chemical control should target the vector only when necessary and according to current recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy disease-free planting material, use resistant or tolerant varieties where available, rogue infected plants early, and manage alternate virus hosts and vectors.

diseases.cause: Serious fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum species, particularly Colletotrichum falcatum.
diseases.symptoms: Leaves may yellow and dry prematurely. Splitting an affected stalk can reveal characteristic reddish internal tissue, often with white patches.
diseases.treatment: Use healthy disease-free setts and resistant or tolerant varieties. Remove diseased clumps and avoid ratooning severely affected crops. Biological or chemical disease-management measures should be selected according to current local sugarcane recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy disease-free setts, plant resistant or tolerant varieties, remove diseased clumps, maintain field sanitation, and avoid planting material from infected fields.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia species.
diseases.symptoms: Small yellowish to brown rust pustules develop on leaves and may produce powdery spores. Severe infection can reduce photosynthetic leaf area.
diseases.treatment: Maintain field sanitation and monitor foliage regularly. Use resistant or tolerant varieties where available. If disease pressure becomes significant, apply only a currently recommended fungicide according to the local sugarcane advisory and product label.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant or tolerant varieties where available, maintain field sanitation, monitor leaves regularly, and avoid planting susceptible material in areas with recurring disease.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Septoria species.
diseases.symptoms: Small chlorotic or brown leaf lesions develop and may enlarge, sometimes producing dark fruiting bodies within lesions. Severe infection can reduce green leaf area.
diseases.treatment: Use healthy seed and suitable varieties, maintain balanced nutrition and manage infected crop residues. Monitor lower leaves early. If fungicide treatment is required, use a currently recommended wheat fungicide according to the local agricultural advisory and current label.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed and suitable varieties, maintain balanced nutrition, manage infected crop residues, avoid excessive crop density, and monitor lower leaves early in the season.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused mainly by Alternaria solani.
diseases.symptoms: Small dark brown to black spots develop on older leaves and gradually enlarge into circular lesions with concentric rings. Severe infection can cause yellowing, leaf drop, and reduced tuber yield.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected plant material where practical and improve field sanitation. Use locally recommended fungicides for early blight when disease pressure warrants treatment, following the current label and local agricultural advisory.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed tubers, maintain balanced plant nutrition, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, provide adequate spacing and field sanitation, and rotate crops where practical.

diseases.cause: Disease caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans.
diseases.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked lesions appear on leaves and stems, often expanding rapidly under cool and humid conditions. White fuzzy growth may develop on the underside of infected leaves, and tubers can develop dark brown to reddish-brown internal rot.
diseases.treatment: Remove and properly dispose of severely infected plant material where practical. Improve field drainage and reduce prolonged leaf wetness. Use locally recommended late-blight fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment, following the current label and local agricultural advisory.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy certified seed tubers, provide good field drainage, avoid excessive irrigation and prolonged leaf wetness, maintain adequate spacing, monitor during cool humid weather, and remove infected material promptly.

diseases.cause: Tuber rot can be caused by several fungal or bacterial pathogens, particularly when tubers are injured, poorly dried, or stored under unsuitable conditions.
diseases.symptoms: Soft or firm brown, dark, or discolored areas develop on potato tubers. Rot may progress internally, sometimes accompanied by softening, decay, unpleasant odour, or secondary infection.
diseases.treatment: Remove and separate rotten or damaged tubers. Dry healthy tubers thoroughly before storage and maintain suitable storage conditions with good ventilation. Avoid storing injured or cut tubers with healthy produce.
diseases.prevention: Handle tubers carefully to prevent wounds, harvest under suitable conditions, allow tubers to dry and cure before storage, maintain clean and well-ventilated storage conditions, and regularly remove damaged or decaying tubers.

diseases.cause: Fungal diseases caused by rust fungi such as Puccinia species.
diseases.symptoms: Orange, yellow, brown, or dark rust-colored pustules develop on leaves and sometimes stems. Severe infection can reduce green leaf area and grain development.
diseases.treatment: Remove heavily affected volunteer plants where practical and use locally recommended rust-management fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment, following the current label and local agricultural advisory.
diseases.prevention: Use rust-resistant varieties where available, sow at the recommended time, maintain balanced nutrition, and monitor fields regularly.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici.
diseases.symptoms: White to gray powdery fungal growth develops on leaves and stems. In severe cases leaves yellow, dry prematurely, and contribute less to grain filling.
diseases.treatment: Improve crop ventilation and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment, following the label.
diseases.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen, maintain appropriate plant density, use resistant varieties where available, and monitor dense crop growth.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Tilletia indica.
diseases.symptoms: Some grains become partially replaced by dark masses of fungal spores and may produce a distinctive fishy or unpleasant odour when crushed.
diseases.treatment: Use clean seed and follow local seed-treatment and disease-management recommendations. Heavily contaminated seed should not be used for planting.
diseases.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, follow quarantine and seed-health regulations, and use resistant or tolerant varieties where available.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Magnaporthe oryzae.
diseases.symptoms: Spindle-shaped gray, brown, or reddish-brown lesions develop on leaves. Lesions may also occur on nodes and panicles, causing poor grain filling.
diseases.treatment: Maintain balanced nitrogen nutrition and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment, following the label.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, use healthy seed, avoid excessive nitrogen, and monitor fields during humid conditions.

diseases.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.
diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked streaks develop along leaf margins and expand into yellow or straw-colored areas. Severely affected leaves may dry from the tip downward.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected plant material where practical and follow local disease-management recommendations. Avoid unnecessary nitrogen application.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, healthy seed, balanced fertilization, good field sanitation, and avoid excessive nitrogen.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Rhizoctonia solani.
diseases.symptoms: Oval or irregular green-gray to brown lesions develop on leaf sheaths near the water line and can spread upward under humid conditions.
diseases.treatment: Improve crop spacing and canopy ventilation and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen, maintain suitable spacing, manage weeds, and monitor dense crop areas.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease commonly associated with Exserohilum turcicum.
diseases.symptoms: Long gray-green to tan or brown lesions develop on leaves and may enlarge and merge, reducing the photosynthetic leaf area.
diseases.treatment: Remove heavily infected residue where practical and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant hybrids where available, rotate crops, maintain field sanitation, and avoid excessive crop density.

diseases.cause: Disease caused by several downy mildew pathogens, including Peronosclerospora species.
diseases.symptoms: Pale yellow or whitish streaks develop on leaves, sometimes with downy growth under humid conditions. Plants may become stunted.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected plants where practical and follow locally recommended disease-management measures.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant seed or hybrids where available, avoid poorly drained fields, and use healthy planting material.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Sporisorium scitamineum.
diseases.symptoms: A long black whip-like structure develops from the growing point of infected plants. Infected plants may become thin and produce excessive side shoots.
diseases.treatment: Remove and safely destroy infected stools where practical and follow local recommendations for disease management.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy disease-free planting material, resistant varieties where available, and inspect seed cane before planting.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Phomopsis vexans.
diseases.symptoms: Dark lesions develop on stems and fruits. Infected fruits may develop sunken spots, internal decay, and black fungal structures.
diseases.treatment: Remove and destroy infected fruits and plant parts and maintain field sanitation. Use locally recommended fungicides when necessary.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, crop rotation, good field sanitation, and avoid prolonged leaf and fruit wetness.

diseases.cause: Bacterial disease commonly caused by Ralstonia solanacearum.
diseases.symptoms: Plants wilt rapidly, often while leaves remain green. Cutting the stem may reveal brown vascular tissue and bacterial ooze under suitable conditions.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected plants and avoid moving contaminated soil or irrigation water to healthy areas. Follow local management recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seedlings, resistant or tolerant varieties where available, crop rotation, good drainage, and clean planting material.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Colletotrichum species.
diseases.symptoms: Sunken dark lesions develop on fruits, sometimes with concentric rings and orange or salmon-colored spore masses. Leaves and stems may also be affected.
diseases.treatment: Remove and destroy infected fruits and plant material and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, avoid overhead irrigation, improve field ventilation, and remove infected fruits promptly.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Leveillula taurica.
diseases.symptoms: Yellow patches develop on upper leaf surfaces with white fungal growth commonly visible on the underside. Severe infection causes premature leaf drop.
diseases.treatment: Improve air circulation and use locally recommended fungicides when required.
diseases.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen, maintain suitable spacing, and monitor crops regularly.

diseases.cause: Fungal diseases caused by Puccinia species.
diseases.symptoms: Rust-colored or dark pustules develop on leaves and stems and can reduce green leaf area and grain production when infection is severe.
diseases.treatment: Use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, sow at the recommended time, and monitor fields regularly.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease commonly associated with Alternaria species.
diseases.symptoms: Dark circular to irregular spots develop on leaves, stems, and pods. Older lesions may show concentric rings.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected residue where practical and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, avoid dense sowing, rotate crops, and maintain field sanitation.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Erysiphe cruciferarum.
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth develops on leaves, stems, and sometimes pods. Severe infection can reduce plant vigour.
diseases.treatment: Improve air circulation and use locally recommended fungicides when necessary.
diseases.prevention: Maintain appropriate spacing, avoid excessive nitrogen, and monitor the crop during favourable weather.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Diplocarpon rosae.
diseases.symptoms: Black or dark circular spots develop on leaves, often followed by yellowing and premature leaf drop.
diseases.treatment: Remove fallen and infected leaves and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Keep foliage dry where possible, improve air circulation, remove fallen leaves, and prune appropriately.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Botrytis cinerea.
diseases.symptoms: Brown lesions and gray fuzzy fungal growth develop on flowers, buds, and tender plant parts, especially under cool humid conditions.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected flowers and plant material and improve ventilation. Use locally recommended fungicides when appropriate.
diseases.prevention: Avoid prolonged flower wetness, provide good spacing, remove spent flowers, and maintain sanitation.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Botrytis cinerea.
diseases.symptoms: Brown water-soaked lesions and gray fungal growth develop on flowers, leaves, and stems under humid conditions.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected flowers and plant material, improve ventilation, and use locally recommended fungicides when necessary.
diseases.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, maintain plant spacing, and remove decaying plant material.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Botrytis species.
diseases.symptoms: Brown or water-soaked spots develop on leaves and flowers, followed by gray fungal growth during humid conditions.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected plant parts and improve air circulation. Use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Avoid prolonged leaf wetness, provide good spacing, and remove infected debris promptly.

diseases.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris.
diseases.symptoms: Yellow to brown V-shaped lesions develop from leaf margins and veins may become dark. Severe leaves can dry and fall.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected plants and follow local bacterial disease-management recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use clean seed, crop rotation, good drainage, and avoid working with plants while foliage is wet.

diseases.cause: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris.
diseases.symptoms: Yellow V-shaped leaf lesions develop from margins and darkening of veins may occur.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected material and maintain field sanitation.
diseases.prevention: Use clean seed, crop rotation, good drainage, and avoid handling wet plants.

diseases.cause: Fungal-like disease caused by Peronospora farinosa f. sp. spinaciae.
diseases.symptoms: Yellow patches develop on upper leaf surfaces with gray-purple growth on the underside under humid conditions.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected leaves and improve ventilation. Use locally recommended products when appropriate.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, increase spacing, improve drainage, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

diseases.cause: Viral disease transmitted mainly by whiteflies.
diseases.symptoms: Veins become bright yellow and the yellowing spreads through the leaf network. Plants may become stunted and produce fewer fruits.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely infected plants where practical and manage whitefly populations according to local agricultural recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy planting material, control whitefly vectors, remove infected plants early, and maintain field sanitation.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Erysiphe pisi.
diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth appears on leaves, stems, and pods. Severe infection can reduce plant vigour and yield.
diseases.treatment: Improve air circulation and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, maintain suitable spacing, and avoid excessive nitrogen.

diseases.cause: Fungal-like disease caused by Peronospora destructor.
diseases.symptoms: Pale green or yellow patches develop on leaves, followed by grayish-purple fungal growth during humid conditions. Leaves may bend and collapse.
diseases.treatment: Improve field ventilation and drainage and use locally recommended disease-management products when necessary.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy bulbs or seedlings, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, maintain spacing, and rotate crops.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria porri.
diseases.symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions develop on leaves and enlarge into purple or brown lesions surrounded by lighter areas.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected debris and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain field sanitation, improve air circulation, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria porri.
diseases.symptoms: Small pale or water-soaked spots enlarge into purple-brown lesions on leaves and can cause premature drying.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected plant debris and use locally recommended fungicides when required.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy planting material, rotate crops, improve air circulation, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

diseases.cause: Soil-borne fungal disease commonly associated with Fusarium species.
diseases.symptoms: Leaves yellow and wilt, roots deteriorate, and the basal plate of bulbs becomes brown or rotted.
diseases.treatment: Remove severely affected plants and improve drainage. Use locally recommended planting-material and disease-management practices.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy cloves, avoid waterlogging, rotate crops, and maintain clean planting material.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria species.
diseases.symptoms: Small dark spots develop on leaves and may enlarge into circular brown lesions with concentric rings.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected leaves and plant debris and use locally recommended fungicides when necessary.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, crop rotation, adequate spacing, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

diseases.cause: Soil-borne disease caused by Plasmodiophora brassicae.
diseases.symptoms: Roots develop enlarged irregular swellings and plants become stunted or wilt during water stress.
diseases.treatment: Remove affected plants and avoid moving contaminated soil to clean fields. Follow local soil-management recommendations.
diseases.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, maintain suitable soil drainage and pH, rotate crops, and use clean planting areas.

diseases.cause: Fungal disease commonly associated with Alternaria dauci and related pathogens.
diseases.symptoms: Small brown spots develop on leaves and enlarge into dark lesions. Severely affected foliage may dry and die back.
diseases.treatment: Remove infected plant debris and use locally recommended fungicides when disease pressure warrants treatment.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy seed, crop rotation, adequate spacing, and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

diseases.cause: Root disease associated with several soil-borne organisms, including Pythium species.
diseases.symptoms: Small sunken brown lesions or cavities develop on carrot roots, reducing market quality.
diseases.treatment: Improve drainage and follow locally recommended soil and crop-management practices.
diseases.prevention: Avoid excessive irrigation, maintain suitable soil drainage, rotate crops, and use healthy seed.

diseases.cause: Botrytis species fungi, favored by cool, humid conditions and prolonged moisture.
diseases.symptoms: Brown or water-soaked spots on leaves and flowers, gray mold growth, and decay of plant tissue.
diseases.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plant parts, improve air circulation, and reduce excess moisture.
diseases.prevention: Use healthy bulbs, provide good spacing and drainage, and avoid prolonged wet foliage.
diseases.severity: Moderate to high if infection spreads rapidly during cool and humid conditions.

diseases.cause: Soil-borne fungal or bacterial pathogens favored by excessive moisture and poor drainage.
diseases.symptoms: Soft or rotting bulbs, poor emergence, yellowing foliage, and weak or dying plants.
diseases.treatment: Remove rotting bulbs, improve drainage, and avoid planting damaged or infected bulbs.
diseases.prevention: Plant healthy bulbs in well-drained soil and avoid excessive irrigation.
diseases.severity: High when infected bulbs are stored or planted in wet conditions.

needs_identification.classification_note: Dataset label 'miner' is ambiguous. Do not publish as a disease until the original image class is identified.

needs_identification.symptoms: Water-soaked to yellowish lesions can develop along the leaf margins and spread along the leaf. Severe infection can cause extensive leaf blighting.
needs_identification.favorable_conditions: Disease risk increases under conditions favorable to bacterial spread, including excessive standing water.
needs_identification.management: Monitor fields regularly, maintain appropriate water management and follow locally recommended integrated disease-management practices.
needs_identification.prevention: Use resistant or tolerant varieties where recommended, maintain balanced crop nutrition, monitor regularly and avoid unnecessary excess nitrogen.
needs_identification.treatment: Follow current locally approved management recommendations from agricultural authorities. Chemical treatment should follow the current product label and local advisory.

needs_identification.classification_note: Dataset label 'Yellow' is insufficient to identify the exact disease.

needs_identification.symptoms: Yellow stripes develop on wheat leaves.
needs_identification.favorable_conditions: Cold temperatures with intermittent rainfall favor stripe-rust development.
needs_identification.management: Regular field monitoring and early detection are important. Use locally recommended resistant varieties where available and follow timely disease-management advisories.
needs_identification.prevention: Use suitable resistant varieties and regularly scout the crop for early symptoms.
needs_identification.treatment: When disease is detected, follow the current fungicide recommendation and product label applicable to the crop and region.
needs_identification.source: ICAR — Stripe Rust (Yellow Rust) of Wheat
